commands.stderr:
flag provided but not defined: -no-such-flag
usage: grain list [flags]

Flags:
  -author string
    	shorthand for -filter author:any:VALUE
  -auto-merge
    	only tasks that merge themselves (-auto-merge=false for only those needing a human)
  -base string
    	shorthand for -filter base:any:VALUE (or "none" for the tasks taking the repo's default)
  -blocked
    	only tasks waiting on another task (-blocked=false for only the unblocked ones)
  -capability string
    	shorthand for -filter capability:any:VALUE (or "none" for the tasks carrying none)
  -closed
    	list closed tasks too (-closed=false to leave them out where the deployment shows them by default)
  -deferred
    	list deferred tasks too
  -filter condition
    	only tasks matching this condition, written attribute:comparison:value -- repeatable, and every one of them has to hold
  -interactive
    	only live chats (-interactive=false for only background tasks)
  -origin string
    	shorthand for -filter origin:any:VALUE (hand, external, proposed, schedule, suite, fix, review)
  -repo string
    	shorthand for -filter repo:any:VALUE (owner/name, or "none" for the tasks with no target repo)
  -search string
    	only tasks whose title or id contains this text, case-insensitively
  -sort order
    	print in this order: attribute:asc or attribute:desc keys, comma-separated, the first deciding and the rest breaking its ties
  -state string
    	shorthand for -filter state:any:VALUE (proposed, queued, running, awaiting_reply, failed, awaiting_submit, completed, deferred, closed, or asked for awaiting_reply and awaiting_submit both)

Conditions (-filter, repeatable) are written attribute:comparison:value, the
spelling the UI writes into a link, so a condition can be pasted between them:

  grain list -filter repo:any:acme/widgets,acme/gadgets -filter created:within:7
  grain list -filter capability:all:gh,gcp -sort state:asc,created:desc
  grain list -filter derived_from:eq:acme/widgets#42 -filter filed_via:has:session=abc123

Several values in one condition are separated by "," or "|"; a value that has
to carry one is written %2C or %7C. "none" is "has no value for this at all".

The fields this deployment declares are attributes too, under custom.<name>,
with the comparisons their declared type takes -- they are listed below when
the deployment can be asked:

  grain list -filter custom.priority:any:high|critical -sort custom.due:asc

Attributes, and the comparisons each takes:
  state        any, none
  repo         any, none, empty, filled
  title        has, hasnot
  capability   any, none, all, empty, filled
  base         any, none, empty, filled
  reads        any, none, all, empty, filled
  writes       any, none, all, empty, filled
  author       any, none, has, hasnot
  creator      any, none, has, hasnot
  user         any, none, has, hasnot
  origin       any, none
  kind         any, none
  autoMerge    any, none
  blocked      any, none
  created      within, after, before, empty, filled
  started      within, after, before, empty, filled
  completed    within, after, before, empty, filled
  merged       within, after, before, empty, filled
  pullRequest  has, hasnot, empty, filled
  review       any, none, empty, filled
  framework    any, none, empty, filled
  dependsOn    any, none, all, empty, filled
  id           has, hasnot
  priority     eq, ne, gt, lt, empty, filled

Comparisons:
  any      is any of
  none     is none of
  all      has all of
  has      contains
  hasnot   does not contain
  eq       is
  ne       is not
  gt       is more than
  lt       is less than
  after    is after
  before   is before
  within   is within the last
  empty    is empty
  filled   is set

-sort takes attribute:asc or attribute:desc keys over the same attributes, and
still answers to the named orders author, backlog, manual, newest, oldest, repo, state, title.
